UPSTREAM: drm/i915/gen9: Get rid of redundant watermark values Now that we've make skl_wm_levels make a little more sense, we can remove all of the redundant wm information. Up until now we'd been storing two copies of all of the skl watermarks: one being the skl_pipe_wm structs, the other being the global wm struct in drm_i915_private containing the raw register values. This is confusing and problematic, since it means we're prone to accidentally letting the two copies go out of sync. So, get rid of all of the functions responsible for computing the register values and just use a single helper, skl_write_wm_level(), to convert and write the new watermarks on the fly. Changes since v1: - Fixup skl_write_wm_level() - Fixup skl_wm_level_from_reg_val() - Don't forget to copy *active to intel_crtc->wm.active.skl Changes since v2: - Fix usage of wrong cstate Changes since v3 (by Paulo): - Rebase Reviewed-by: Maarten Lankhorst <maarten.lankhorst@linux.intel.com> Reviewed-by: Paulo Zanoni <paulo.r.zanoni@intel.com> (v2) Cc: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Cc: Matt Roper <matthew.d.roper@intel.com> Cc: Paulo Zanoni <paulo.r.zanoni@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Lyude <cpaul@redhat.com> Signed-off-by: Paulo Zanoni <paulo.r.zanoni@intel.com> Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/1476814189-6062-1-git-send-email-paulo.r.zanoni@intel.com (cherry picked from commit d8c0fafcbd68eb3506fec3638e7d77a1a55b1121) from drm-intel-next-2016-10-24 Signed-off-by: Tarun <tarun.vyas@intel.com> BUG=b:36446508 TEST=No regressions in KBL and APL based devices Change-Id: I5ad7fbbc546c305ee2a4d20eac7f81998b166f37 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/536883 Commit-Ready: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Tested-by: Casey G Bowman <casey.g.bowman@intel.com> Tested-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@google.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@google.com>

UPSTREAM: drm/i915: Respect alternate_aux_channel for all DDI ports The VBT provides the platform a way to mix and match the DDI ports vs. AUX channels. Currently we only trust the VBT for DDI E, which has no corresponding AUX channel of its own. However it is possible that some board might use some non-standard DDI vs. AUX port routing even for the other ports. Perhaps for signal routing reasons or something, So let's generalize this and trust the VBT for all ports. For now we'll limit this to DDI platforms, as we trust the VBT a bit more there anyway when it comes to the DDI ports. I've structured the code in a way that would allow us to easily expand this to other platforms as well, by simply filling in the ddi_port_info. v2: Drop whitespace changes, keep MISSING_CASE() for unknown aux ch assignment, include a commit message, include debug message during init Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org Cc: Maarten Maathuis <madman2003@gmail.com> Tested-by: Maarten Maathuis <madman2003@gmail.com> References: https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=97877 Signed-off-by: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/1476208368-5710-2-git-send-email-ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com Reviewed-by: Jim Bride <jim.bride@linux.intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 8f7ce038f1178057733b7e765bf9160a2f9be14b) from drm-intel-next-2016-10-24 Signed-off-by: Tarun <tarun.vyas@intel.com> BUG=b:36446508 TEST=No regressions in KBL and APL based devices Change-Id: Ib1ea07081d094d7e2e67d3d4f454ccf401832bc4 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/536889 Commit-Ready: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Tested-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Tested-by: Casey G Bowman <casey.g.bowman@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@google.com>

cr50: always use /dev/tpm0 to communicate with Cr50 With upcoming removal of USB interface connection between AP and H1, and after verifying that both I2C and SPI interfaces are reliable, there is no need to use different channels to communicate with H1 on different devices. Let's use /dev/tpm0 everywhere, this means there is no more need to honor the h1_over_spi USE flag and to edit the startup script to change the mode between USB and /dev/tpm0. power: Add D-Bus API to ignore the power button Add the IgnoreNextPowerButtonPress D-Bus method to ignore the next press of the power button. This masking is active until the power button release or the timeout set when invoking the method. This will be used by the integrated second-factor authentication to avoid spurious UI actions when the power button is used as the user physical presence sensing method. BUG=b:35545754 TEST=run unit-tests and manually: dbus-send --type=method_call --system --dest=org.chromium.PowerManager /org/chromium/PowerManager org.chromium.PowerManager.IgnoreNextPowerButtonPress int64:10000000 CQ-DEPEND=CL:544296 Change-Id: Idac5e46166081f27a843b461458c5ec1a29a8b9b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/541304 Commit-Ready: Vincent Palatin <vpalatin@chromium.org> Tested-by: Vincent Palatin <vpalatin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>
